name: Harumaf
title: Wall Builder in Jerusalem
summary: Harumaf was one of those who participated in the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls under Nehemiah's leadership. He is mentioned in Nehemiah 3:10 as the father of Jedaiah, who repaired the wall directly opposite his own house. Harumaf represents the faithful Jews who returned from exile and helped restore the city.

keyEvents.title: Rebuilding of Jerusalem's Wall
keyEvents.description: Harumaf is mentioned as the father of Jedaiah, who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall directly opposite his own house during Nehemiah's wall-building project.

keyEvents.title: The Community's Effort for the Walls
keyEvents.description: Harumaf and his family were part of a larger community of Jewish families and leaders who together rebuilt Jerusalem's walls after the exile.

keyEvents.title: Nehemiah's Inspection of the Walls
keyEvents.description: Before the rebuilding work began, Nehemiah inspected the ruined walls at night and mobilized the people for the task.

keyEvents.title: Opposition to the Rebuilding
keyEvents.description: The workers, including families like Harumaph's, faced opposition from Sanballat, Tobiah, and other enemies, but continued despite the threats.

keyEvents.title: Completion of the Wall
keyEvents.description: Despite opposition, the wall was completed in 52 days, a testament to the cooperation among all the families who participated in the work.
